To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) chronic intermittent cocaine treatment induces the expression of FOS-related proteins that persist after the drug treatment has ended; 2) these proteins are expressed in the striatum; 3) the persistent expression of some of these proteins requires dopamine D1-class receptors; and 4) the persistent expression requires the presence of cocaine in the environment.
the D1‐class receptors in the striatum are required for the expression of Fras that persist after chronic intermittent cocaine treatment.
chronic intermittent administration of cocaine induces the persistent expression of Fras in the striatum that is dependent on the activation of D1- class dopamine receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the persistent expression of proteins in the striatum in response to repeated drug exposure.
the role of D1- class dopamine receptors in the expression of Fras following chronic exposure to cocaine.
the molecular and behavioral consequences of chronic exposure to psychomotors stimulants.

chronic intermittent administration of cocaine induces a persistent expression of proteins that are dependent on dopamine D1-class receptors and a persistent expression of other proteins that are independent of dopamine D1-class activation.

the D1‐class dopamine receptor influences the persistent expression of Fras in the striatum, but that the D1- class dopamine receptor does not regulate the induction of Fras in this brain region.
